slides.title: What is the Better Curriculum: Controller-Shaped Grasping Behavior for Contact Force-Sensitive Manipulation
slides.tldr: TACTILE REFLEX CONTROLLER FOR DATA COLLECTION
slides.highlight: This research introduces a tactile reflex controller to generate high-quality demonstrations for force-sensitive manipulation, enabling policies to achieve 95% stable grasps on fragile objects.

card.one_liner: Tactile reflex controllers improve fragile-object grasping by shaping demonstrations for tactile-free policy learning.
card.key_idea: A 25Hz tactile reflex controller acts as a collection-time teacher, producing stable, controller-shaped demonstrations that a vision-only student policy learns to reproduce without tactile input.
card.evaluation: Tested on ACT and $\pi_{0.5}$ using fragile plastic cups; reflex-data policies achieved 95% stability versus 5-15% for manual-data baselines.
card.limitation: Tactile-free policies fail under external disturbances, requiring a decoupled high-rate tactile arbiter for reliable grasp retention.

slides.title: EmbodiedSWE: Coding Agents for Long Horizon Dexterous Robotics
slides.tldr: CODING AGENTS PROVIDING SCALABLE SUPERVISION FOR ROBOT POLICIES
slides.highlight: This research introduces a benchmark and framework using coding agents to solve complex, long-horizon dexterous tasks and convert those solutions into diverse training data for VLAs.

card.one_liner: Coding agents solve complex robotic tasks and generate diverse simulation data to train generalist VLA policies.
card.key_idea: EmbodiedSWE-Bench evaluates agents writing robot code; EmbodiedSWE-Gen then diversifies these verified solutions (scene, strategy, phase, noise) into scalable training trajectories for VLA finetuning.
card.evaluation: Tested on 28 long-horizon tasks across 5 embodiments. VLA success rose from 18% to 69% with more data; demonstrated sim-to-real transfer on real robots.
card.limitation: Solutions require substantial iterative interaction and are typically specialized to individual task instances.

slides.title: VisForce: Visual Grounding of Current and Desired Forces for Goal-Conditioned Dexterous Manipulation
slides.tldr: VISUAL GROUNDING OF CONTACT FORCES FOR DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: VisForce introduces a method to visually ground current and desired forces at fingertip locations, enabling force-aware actions in VLA-based dexterous manipulation.

card.one_liner: VisForce visually grounds current and desired forces at fingertip locations to improve dexterous robotic manipulation.
card.key_idea: Renders actuator and desired forces as visual cues on wrist and goal images, fusing them via goal-conditioned cross-attention within a VLA model.
card.evaluation: Tested on UR10 with RH56F1 hand across grasping and multi-stage tasks; achieved up to 80% success in force-sensitive grasping and 70% in cup insertion.

slides.title: Res-HIL: Human-Guided Residual Reinforcement Learning for Sample-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation
slides.tldr: HUMAN-GUIDED RESIDUAL RL FOR DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: Res-HIL introduces a framework that learns corrective actions on top of a frozen imitation policy using human interventions for direct supervision and reward shaping. This approach improves sample efficiency and performance in contact-rich manipulation tasks compared to full-policy RL.

card.one_liner: Res-HIL improves pretrained manipulation policies using human interventions for residual RL and reward shaping.
card.key_idea: Learns a residual policy atop a frozen imitation base, using human interventions for direct supervision (BC loss) and decaying penalties to shape sparse rewards.
card.evaluation: Tested on five contact-rich tasks (e.g., peg-in-hole, cable routing) against HIL-SERL and ResFiT; Res-HIL showed superior success rates and faster convergence.

slides.title: Contact-Implicit Stein Projected ADMM for Discovery of Diverse Contact-Rich Manipulation Strategies
slides.highlight: This research introduces a solver combining Consensus ADMM with Stein variational inference to discover multiple distinct contact-rich solutions for tasks like pushing and grasping.

card.one_liner: Stein Projected ADMM discovers diverse, feasible contact-rich manipulation strategies by injecting repulsion into split variables.
card.key_idea: Combines Stein Variational Gradient Descent with ADMM, applying the repulsive force to the split variable $z$ before projecting onto the feasible set to maintain diversity and feasibility.
card.evaluation: Tested on annulus/complementarity problems and tasks (pushing, grasping, pivoting, handover) against SteinSQP and ADMM. Results show better diversity and faster convergence.

slides.title: BEE: Intervention-Adaptive Real-World Reinforcement Learning with Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.highlight: BEE introduces a framework for real-world RL on frozen VLA models that uses human corrections to set per-dimension constraints on policy optimization. This is relevant to MIMIC's focus on agent models and the integration of human-AI interaction for complex tasks.

card.one_liner: Bee uses uncertainty-aware human corrections to constrain real-world RL for precision-critical VLA manipulation tasks.
card.key_idea: A Correction Model predicts per-dimension variance of human interventions, creating a Mahalanobis constraint that keeps the policy close to consistent corrections while allowing exploration in variable dimensions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three real-world tasks and one LIBERO-Pro simulation; Bee achieved 91.2% average success rate, outperforming RLT (57.5%) and DSRL (42.1%).
card.limitation: Predicted uncertainty is less reliable when human corrections are sparse.

slides.title: TactileStep: Sole Tactile Learning for Regulating Foot-Terrain Interaction in Humanoid Locomotion
slides.highlight: TactileStep introduces a tactile learning framework that uses sole pressure sensing to achieve softer touchdowns and more stable support in humanoid robots, contributing to the embodied learning goals of RwB.

card.one_liner: TactileStep uses sole-pressure sensing to enable softer landings and more stable stance in humanoid locomotion.
card.key_idea: A framework aligning simulated and real tactile features (force, contact area, CoP) with phase-aware RL rewards to regulate foot-terrain interaction across four gait phases.
card.evaluation: Tested in simulation and on a Unitree G1; reduced peak touchdown force by 48.8% and noise by 30.1 dB over a perceptive baseline.
card.limitation: Untested on deformable surfaces, high-speed motions, or long-term sensor durability; relies on hand-designed gait phase estimation.

slides.title: LiMA: Bridging Long-term Imagination to Real-time Dexterous Manipulation via Asynchronous Diffusion
slides.tldr: ASYNCHRONOUS DUAL-SYSTEM FRAMEWORK FOR DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: LiMA decouples long-horizon intent planning from high-frequency motion refinement to reduce inference latency and improve success rates in bimanual dexterous manipulation.

card.one_liner: LiMA decouples long-term imagination from real-time execution to enable efficient, high-frequency bimanual dexterous manipulation.
card.key_idea: An asynchronous dual-system framework using a 'Future Dreamer' for sparse intent and a 'Motion Refiner' linked via a Latent Schrödinger Bridge for dense action refinement.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on six real-world bimanual tasks; achieved 70.8% overall success rate and 45.8% lower latency than Cosmos-Policy using an NVIDIA H100 GPU.
card.limitation: Performance degrades under severe visual occlusion or low visual variance due to reliance on camera inputs without tactile feedback.
